hypothesis: What if adult TTC pay-as-you-go fare rose by CAD 0.50 in a small UTSC-area district?
retrieval_query: fare increase ridership mode shift shopping retail employment

selected_claims.finding: Bogota BRT fare-increase response differed by horizon and income/off-peak use; reported short-run elasticities were about -0.565 at one week and -0.408 after one month.
selected_claims.transfer_warning: Illustrative sensitivity only; not a Toronto fare elasticity.

selected_claims.finding: A Boston low-income fare discount increased trips and health/social-service trips in a randomized evaluation.
selected_claims.transfer_warning: Discount result cannot be reversed mechanically into a Toronto fare-hike effect.

selected_claims.finding: Temporary free public transport had no statistically significant effect on paid hours or earnings.
selected_claims.transfer_warning: Counterevidence to a deterministic worker-income chain.

selected_claims.finding: An Albany downtown fare-free program was associated with positive sales effects for some shop types/seasons and locations near bus routes.
selected_claims.transfer_warning: Fare removal and old downtown context; no Toronto sales coefficient or business-closure probability.

selected_claims.finding: Other off-peak free-fare experiments raised ridership without noticeable commercial or employment change.
selected_claims.transfer_warning: Include zero retail/employment effect as a plausible scenario.

conflicting_claims.resolution: Do not select a positive retail coefficient from these papers; run zero and nonzero illustrative scenarios.
